reference: Independent jq comparisons cover selected values, presence, types, byte lengths, keys and sorted compact serialization without a trailing newline. The documented UTF-8 byte length uses jq utf8bytelength. Strict duplicate-key rejection and TYPE PATH VALUE parse output use separate documented contract expectations; they are not claims of identical jq behavior.
coverage: Bash builtin availability, help metadata entries, and parse output contract
Nested object and array-index get paths
has presence semantics including present-null and absent nested member
Object keys in already sorted ASCII order
Array, object, and UTF-8 string lengths
Nested set with a string replacement
Strict duplicate-key rejection against jq's last-value behavior
exclusions: String length is the documented UTF-8 byte count, not jq Unicode character count. Strict duplicate-key rejection remains a separately checked contract.
The historical jq.sh wrapper is not part of this repository; the current jq builtin receives its own suite.

cases.purpose: Check that Bash reports bashjson as a builtin, that help includes the parser description and parse/validate entries, and that parse emits the documented root and child TYPE PATH VALUE rows.
cases.script:
kind=$(type -t bashjson)
help_text=$(help bashjson)
[[ $kind == builtin ]] || exit 1
[[ $help_text == *"JSON parser/serializer"* ]] || exit 1
[[ $help_text == *"bashjson parse"* ]] || exit 1
[[ $help_text == *"bashjson validate"* ]] || exit 1
printf 'builtin\nhelp metadata available\n'
printf '%s\n' '{"a":1}' | bashjson parse
cases.stdout:
builtin
help metadata available
object . {"a":1}
number .a 1

cases.purpose: Compare nested object lookup and a chained array-index/object-field lookup on the same compact JSON document.
cases.script:
doc='{"account":{"profile":{"score":17}},"records":[{"name":"Ari"},{"name":"Mira"}]}'
if [[ $(type -t bashjson) == builtin ]]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$doc" | bashjson get .account.profile.score
  printf '%s\n' "$doc" | bashjson get '.records[1].name'
else
  printf '%s\n' "$doc" | jq -c '.account.profile.score'
  printf '%s\n' "$doc" | jq -c '.records[1].name'
fi

cases.purpose: Check that a present null-valued field exists and a missing nested field does not, matching jq has predicates.
cases.script:
doc='{"nullable":null,"nested":{"found":1}}'
if [[ $(type -t bashjson) == builtin ]]; then
  if printf '%s
' "$doc" | bashjson has .nullable; then printf 'present-null
'; else exit 1; fi
  if printf '%s
' "$doc" | bashjson has .nested.missing; then exit 1; else printf 'missing-nested
'; fi
else
  if printf '%s
' "$doc" | jq -e 'has("nullable")' >/dev/null; then printf 'present-null
'; else exit 1; fi
  if printf '%s
' "$doc" | jq -e '(.nested | has("missing"))' >/dev/null; then exit 1; else printf 'missing-nested
'; fi
fi

cases.purpose: Compare type results for string, number, boolean, null, array, and object values.
cases.script:
doc='{"s":"x","n":1,"b":true,"z":null,"a":[],"o":{}}'
if [[ $(type -t bashjson) == builtin ]]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$doc" | bashjson type .s
  printf '%s\n' "$doc" | bashjson type .n
  printf '%s\n' "$doc" | bashjson type .b
  printf '%s\n' "$doc" | bashjson type .z
  printf '%s\n' "$doc" | bashjson type .a
  printf '%s\n' "$doc" | bashjson type .o
else
  printf '%s\n' "$doc" | jq -r '(.s, .n, .b, .z, .a, .o) | type'
fi

cases.purpose: Compare object key output where source order is already jq's lexicographic key order. Both commands emit unquoted key names, one per line.
cases.script:
doc='{"alpha":1,"bravo":2}'
if [[ $(type -t bashjson) == builtin ]]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$doc" | bashjson keys .
else
  printf '%s\n' "$doc" | jq -r 'keys[]'
fi

cases.purpose: Compare the documented UTF-8 byte length with jq utf8bytelength; array and object lengths use their shared length interface.
cases.script:
doc='{"label":"é","array":[1,2],"object":{"x":1,"y":2}}'
if [[ $(type -t bashjson) == builtin ]]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$doc" | bashjson length .label
  printf '%s\n' "$doc" | bashjson length .array
  printf '%s\n' "$doc" | bashjson length .object
else
  printf '%s\n' "$doc" | jq -r '.label | utf8bytelength'
  printf '%s\n' "$doc" | jq -r '.array | length'
  printf '%s\n' "$doc" | jq -r '.object | length'
fi

cases.purpose: Replace a nested string value and compare the complete resulting JSON document. The input includes a final newline, which bashjson preserves and jq -c also emits.
cases.script:
doc='{"user":{"name":"old","active":true},"count":1}'
if [[ $(type -t bashjson) == builtin ]]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$doc" | bashjson set .user.name '"new"'
else
  printf '%s\n' "$doc" | jq -c '.user.name = "new"'
fi

cases.purpose: Validate a standard nested JSON document without producing output.
cases.script:
doc='{"ok":true,"list":[null,1,"x"]}'
if [[ $(type -t bashjson) == builtin ]]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$doc" | bashjson validate
else
  printf '%s\n' "$doc" | jq empty
fi

cases.purpose: Compare sorted compact output with jq join-output mode, including the absence of a trailing newline.
cases.script:
doc='{"z":{"n":3,"a":1},"b":[true,{"y":2,"x":4}]}'
if [[ $(type -t bashjson) == builtin ]]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$doc" | bashjson canonical
else
  printf '%s\n' "$doc" | jq -c -S -j .
fi

cases.purpose: The documented strict default rejects duplicate object keys without emitting a canonical document.
Verify that strict validation rejects a leading-zero JSON number, forbidden by RFC 8259 section 6.
The explicit lenient validation option accepts duplicate keys, matching jq validation.
cases.script: if [[ $(type -t bashjson 2>/dev/null) == builtin ]]; then printf '%s' '{"x":1,"x":2}' | bashjson --no-strict-json validate; else printf '%s' '{"x":1,"x":2}' | jq empty; fi
